record.paper_title: Some open problems on best approximation in normed linear spaces
record.context_brief: Existence of separable Banach spaces with no Chebyshev subspace
record.original_question: Does there exist a separable Banach space that has no Chebyshev subspace at all, meaning no linear subspace G for which every point of the ambient space has a unique best approximation in G?

evidence.quote: Does there exist a separable Banach space which has no Cebysev subspace ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X, \|\cdot\|)$ be a real normed linear space. For a nonempty subset $G \subseteq X$ and a point $x \in X$, a best approximation to $x$ from $G$ is an element $g_0 \in G$ such that $\|x - g_0\| = \inf_{g \in G} \|x - g\|$. The set $G$ is called a Chebyshev subspace if $G$ is a linear subspace of $X$ and every point $x \in X$ has exactly one best approximation in $G$.

Question: Does there exist a separable (infinite-dimensional) Banach space $X$ which has no Chebyshev subspace whatsoever — i.e., such that for every linear subspace $G \subseteq X$ there exists some $x \in X$ that fails to have a unique best approximation in $G$?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not yield a definitive resolution. Results indicate that in many separable Banach spaces (e.g., those that are locally uniformly convex or have the Radon–Nikodym property), "almost all" closed subspaces are almost Chebyshev, but no source explicitly settles whether some separable Banach space can fail to admit any Chebyshev subspace at all. The status of the problem is therefore not clearly established from accessible sources.

status_evidence.snippet: Definitions and classical results on Chebyshev sets and subspaces in normed spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the standard definitions but does not resolve the existence question.

status_evidence.title: On almost Chebyshev subspaces
status_evidence.snippet: In separable Banach spaces with LUR norm or RNP, 'almost all' closed subspaces are almost Chebyshev.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates partial positive results in special classes of separable Banach spaces, but does not settle the general question.
